anchors: Never write through it from the host
decision: De-identifying a restored CT leaves a /var/lib/dbus/machine-id symlink alone (never writing through it from the host) and rewrites /etc/mailname and postfix myhostname.

evidence.text: A de-cloned CT still named the base host in postfix and mailname, and its dbus machine-id was a symlink to /etc/machine-id.

reopen_if: pct restore starts regenerating machine and mail identity itself.
why: The symlink's absolute target resolves to the host's own machine-id from the host, and the mail identity is not rewritten by the hostname, so a copy mails as the source.

decision: A running VM with tpmstate0 is copied by the snapshot plus zfs send route; the manual qm create leaves smbios1 and vmgenid out so they are generated fresh.

evidence.text: qemu-server 9.2.15 API2/Qemu.pm dies 'cannot clone TPM state while VM is running' for a full clone of a running VM without snapname; qm create generates smbios1 uuid and vmgenid when absent (same file).

reopen_if: qm clone learns to copy TPM state of a running VM.
why: qm clone --full without a snapshot refuses a running VM with TPM state, and copying smbios1 or vmgenid makes the clone the same machine to the guest.

anchors: Once it exists, `pct set --nameserver` and the GUI DNS tab change nothing inside the CT
decision: PVE rewrites a CT's resolv.conf, hosts and hostname at every start; a regular file /etc/.pve-ignore.<name> stops it, after which pct set --nameserver no longer reaches the file.

evidence.text: pve-container 6.1.20 Setup/Base.pm: ct_is_file_ignored returns -f "$path/.pve-ignore.$name"; set_dns calls ct_modify_file on /etc/resolv.conf, which returns early when ignored.

reopen_if: pve-container stops checking ct_is_file_ignored with a regular-file test, or stops rewriting these files at start.
why: A config-management copy otherwise holds only until the next start (a stop-mode backup included), and the inert pct set afterwards is the half nobody expects.

anchors: On a ZFS subvol `size=0` means NO limit
decision: A full CT clone from a ZFS subvol without refquota shows size=0T, which means no limit; read the config back and set a size with pct resize if one is wanted.

evidence.text: pve-container LXC.pm copy_volume sets size from volume_size_info; ZFSPoolPlugin reports a subvol with refquota none as size 0 and creates a size-0 subvol with refquota=none.

reopen_if: pct clone starts taking the size from the source config rather than the dataset.
why: pct clone sizes the copy from the source dataset's refquota, so a cleared quota surfaces as an alarming 0T that is really unlimited.

anchors: so divert BEFORE installing docker or `systemctl restart docker` afterwards
decision: In an unprivileged CT the apparmor_parser divert goes in before docker is installed, or dockerd is restarted after it.

evidence.text: A hook that installed docker.io then diverted left every docker run failing with the AppArmor profile error until systemctl restart docker.

reopen_if: dockerd re-probes AppArmor per container start.
why: dockerd decides at its own start whether AppArmor is usable, and apt starts it on install, so a later divert is listed but has no effect until a restart.

anchors: `qm status` and the lock cannot tell. A lock records only PVE's own operations
decision: A qm lock or qm status cannot tell whether a test harness or script is driving a VM; ask the tool's own record before stopping, resetting or restoring it.

evidence.text: Queued incident 2026-11-09: six samples of qm status and lock taken mid-arm of an E2E run were identical to an idle VM. locks.md: online migrations, snapshots and backups set a lock. RED (text check): the pre-edit table said only 'Check lock' and never named external use.

reopen_if: PVE gains a lock or status field that external tools set.
why: A lock records only PVE's own operations; an externally driven VM reads running, unlocked, with no active task, exactly like an idle one, so a do-not-cycle check built on the lock passes while a harness is mid-run.

anchors: create a NEW tap (new ifindex), so it is gone with no error
decision: tc state on a guest's tap lives as long as the QEMU process: qm reboot, stop/start, migration and host reboot recreate the tap and drop it, a guest-internal reboot keeps it. Re-apply from a post-start hookscript (never pre-start) with an idempotent apply.

evidence.text: PVE 9.1: qm reboot 900 ran a qmreboot then a qmstart task; tap900i0 ifindex went 9 -> 41, the post-start hookscript logged 'fw-cake: applied on tap900i0' 5 s after the start task, both redirects back; IFB qdisc counters kept counting. tc filter replace without a fixed handle failed 'RTNETLINK: File exists' on a second run. Guest-internal reboot keeping the tap and reboot: 0 are argued from qm's reboot option, not measured. RED: haiku answered that qm reboot keeps the filters.

reopen_if: PVE keeps the QEMU process or the tap across qm reboot, or gains a native per-NIC tc/shaper setting that persists across starts.
why: A shaper or redirect on a VM tap disappears silently at the next qm reboot while the VM looks healthy, so the shaping stops with no error; a weak model believes qm reboot keeps the QEMU process and the filters.
